# awpool

> The free half of the elastic work pool: dispatches public-safe work onto the free GitHub-hosted runners of the public aw* mirrors, so their idle CI minutes become compute. awrun remains the paid/self-hosted lane; this is its free twin.

The monorepo's hosted runners are billing-dead and its self-hosted pool is CPU-bound, while the public mirrors run free hosted CI that only ever executes their own sync and publish lanes. The capacity is real and not pooled: nothing routes monorepo public-safe work to it.

## Install

```
pip install awpool
```

## Use it in 30 seconds

Dispatch one public-safe job to a public mirror's free runner and watch it execute.

## Composes with

- [awrun](https://aitherium.github.io/awrun/) — A priority-aware queue and dispatcher for agentic runs and ad-hoc CI builds. It also judges whether the runner pool is big enough for the queue it is draining, and can ask a host to grow it -- reserving capacity is zero-sum, so a saturated pool needs more of it, not a different share of it.
- [awnet](https://aitherium.github.io/awnet/) — The agentic web — agents host a mesh, and agents join one.
- [awdk](https://aitherium.github.io/awdk/) — Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.

## Where it lives

- Repo: https://github.com/Aitherium/awpool

This repository is mirrored from the AitherOS monorepo by `.github/workflows/sync-awpool.yml`; hand edits made here are overwritten on the next sync — change the source instead.

Everything Aitherium, in one file for agents: https://aitherium.com/llms.txt
